tests.title: The repository is read from every remote URL shape
given: https, ssh and scp-style URLs for one repository, with and without a .git suffix and with and without userinfo
a nested GitLab group path and a URL naming no repository
tests.when: the repository is read from each
then: the three shapes for one repository yield the same host, owner and name
the .git suffix and the userinfo are removed
the nested path yields the full namespace as the owner
the URL naming no repository yields none
tests.pseudocode: in the forge target test file, table over (url, expectedHostOwnerName)

tests.title: The forge and its API URL are derived from the host or the setting
given: hosts github.com, a self-hosted GitHub host and a GitLab host
API URL settings naming each forge, one with and one without the version suffix, and one with surrounding whitespace and a trailing slash
tests.when: the forge and API URL are derived for each
then: github.com yields GitHub and the public API URL
the other hosts yield their documented default paths
a setting naming a forge overrides the host
a GitLab setting gains the version suffix when it lacks one, and whitespace and trailing slashes are ignored
tests.pseudocode: in the forge target test file, table over (host, setting, expectedForge, expectedApiUrl)

tests.title: An unidentifiable forge is refused without a request
given: a workspace whose host names neither forge and which has no API URL setting, and one whose remote URL names no repository
tests.when: a read route and a write route are called for each
then: each answers 422 with error_type forge_unknown
no network request is made in any case
tests.pseudocode: in the forge target test file: assert get(issues).json.error.error_type == 'forge_unknown' and outbound.requests == 0

tests.title: The workspace's credential is sent, never the caller's
given: a workspace holding a distinctive token, a caller holding a different one, and an environment token for the forge
tests.when: a read and a write are made, and once with the workspace holding no credential
then: the forge receives the workspace's token in every case
it never receives the caller's token
a write never carries the environment's token
with no stored credential the request carries no token
tests.pseudocode: in the forge client integration test file: call(read, caller=tokenB); assert forge.lastAuth == workspaceToken

tests.title: The upstream target uses the upstream URL, credential and setting
given: a carry_patch workspace with an upstream URL, an upstream credential and an upstream API URL setting
a standard workspace and a carry_patch workspace with an empty upstream URL
tests.when: a read and a write are called with the target upstream against each, and once with a target of ORIGIN and once with an empty target
then: the carry_patch workspace's calls reach the upstream repository with the upstream credential and the upstream API URL
the upstream API URL setting does not fall back to the origin's when it is empty
the standard and empty-upstream workspaces answer 400 workspace_mode_mismatch
ORIGIN and the empty target answer 400
tests.pseudocode: in the forge client integration test file, table over (workspaceKind, target, expected)

tests.title: Nothing is cached and every request carries the hub's rules
given: a workspace whose credential and API URL setting are changed between two calls
a forge that redirects to another host and one that never answers
tests.when: two calls are made across the change, and calls are made against the redirecting and the silent forges
then: the second call uses the new credential and the new setting
every outbound request carries the hub's user agent
the cross-host redirect answers 502 forge_error
the call exceeding 30 seconds answers 504 forge_timeout
tests.pseudocode: in the forge client integration test file: call(); rotate(); call(); assert forge.lastAuth == newToken; assert call(redirecting).json.error.error_type == 'forge_error'

tests.title: The forge description answers without contacting the forge
given: an active workspace, an archived one, one with an unclassifiable host, a carry_patch workspace with an upstream, and a recording forge
tests.when: the description route is requested for each
then: each answers 200 with forge, api_url, repository, credential and upstream
no request reaches the forge
the unclassifiable host is reported as unknown with a null API URL rather than refused
the archived workspace is answered
the webhook block reports whether the secret exists, the ingress URL or null, and the last delivery time, and carries no secret
tests.pseudocode: in the forge status integration test file: r = get(forge); assert forge.requests == 0 and 'secret' not in r.json.webhook

tests.title: An invalid API URL setting and a failed store are refused
given: settings that are relative, http, carry userinfo, carry a query and carry a fragment
a secrets store and a delivery log made to raise
tests.when: the description route is requested for each
then: each invalid setting answers 422 with error_type forge_api_url_invalid
each message names the setting and the rule and not the value
each failing store answers 500 with no partial body
tests.pseudocode: in the forge status test file, table over the invalid settings asserting 422 and that the value is absent from the message

tests.title: The nine read routes return the documented shapes
given: a stub GitHub and a stub GitLab holding a repository, issues, comments, a pull request, its files, checks and reviews
an archived workspace
tests.when: each read route is called against each forge, and once against the archived workspace
then: each answers 200 with the documented type
every list is a bare array and is empty rather than null when there is nothing
the archived workspace is served
tests.pseudocode: in the forge reads integration test file, table over (route, forgeKind) asserting the response shape

tests.title: Only the issue-list parameters the caller gave are sent
given: a recording forge
tests.when: the issue list is called with no parameters, with each parameter alone, with a labels value containing empty items, and with every parameter together
then: a parameter the caller omitted appears in no outbound request
the limit is always sent and defaults to 30
the labels value drops empty items and is sent only if any remain
tests.pseudocode: in the forge reads test file, table over (givenParams, expectedOutboundParams)

tests.title: An issue thread reports truncation and a comments failure
given: an issue with more comments than are read in one request, and a forge that answers the issue and then fails the comments
tests.when: the issue thread is read in each case
then: the truncated thread says so
the failing-comments case answers 200 with the issue, an empty comment list and the comments' error
that error carries no token and no URL userinfo
tests.pseudocode: in the forge reads integration test file: r = get(issue_thread); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.comments_err and TOKEN not in r.text

tests.title: Bad path numbers and query values are refused before the forge
given: a recording forge
tests.when: read routes are called with a path number of 0, -1, abc and 1.5, and the issue list with a bad state, a limit of 0 and of 101, an empty state and a repeated state
then: each answers 400 with a message beginning with the parameter's name or saying the number must be a positive decimal integer
no request reaches the forge
tests.pseudocode: in the forge reads test file, table over the bad values asserting 400 and forge.requests == 0

tests.title: The nine write routes make their change and answer as documented
given: a stub GitHub and a stub GitLab, and an active workspace the caller may write
tests.when: each write route is called with a valid body against each forge
then: each answers the status its entry gives: 201 for a created issue, pull request or comment, 200 for an update, a close and an existing label, and 204 for the two label routes
each change is visible on the stub forge afterwards
one forge write event is recorded for each
tests.pseudocode: in the forge writes integration test file, table over (route, forgeKind) asserting the status and the forge's state

tests.title: An issue update changes only what it names and refuses an empty change
given: an issue with a title, a body, labels and assignees
tests.when: updates set the title alone, the body to empty, the labels to a new set, the assignees to an empty array, a field to null, no updatable field at all, and on GitLab only the assignees
then: each named field changes and the others do not
an empty body clears the body and an empty array removes every label or assignee
a null field is left alone
the empty update and the GitLab assignees-only update answer 400 nothing to update
tests.pseudocode: in the forge writes test file, table over the update bodies asserting the forge's resulting issue

tests.title: A close with a comment posts the comment first
given: a forge that accepts both, one that refuses the comment, one that accepts the comment and refuses the close, and an already closed issue
tests.when: the close route is called with a non-blank comment against each, and once with no comment and once with a blank one
then: the accepting case posts the comment and then closes
the refused comment leaves the issue open and is answered with the comment's error
the failed close leaves the comment in place, is answered with the close's error and records the comment's URL
no body and a blank comment close without commenting
the already closed issue answers 200
tests.pseudocode: in the forge writes integration test file, table over the five cases asserting the forge's state and the recorded event

tests.title: A label removal answers 204 whether or not the issue had the label
given: an issue with the label, one without it, a forge answering not found for the removal with the issue still present, and one where the issue is gone
tests.when: the removal is called in each case, and with label names containing a slash, a colon and a dot
then: the first two answer 204
the not-found-with-issue-present case re-reads the issue once and answers 204
the missing issue answers 404 forge_not_found
each name is taken from the last path segment decoded exactly once
tests.pseudocode: in the forge writes integration test file, table over the cases asserting the status and the number of forge reads

tests.title: Ensuring a label never changes one that exists
given: a label that exists with a known colour and description, a label that does not, and a forge that refuses the create because a concurrent call just made it
tests.when: the label create is called with a different colour and description in each case, and twice in a row
then: the existing label answers 200 as the forge holds it, with its colour and description untouched
the missing label is created and answers 201
the raced create is followed by one more read and answers 200
calling twice is harmless and both exit successfully
tests.pseudocode: in the forge writes integration test file, table over the three cases asserting the status and the forge's stored label

tests.title: A pull request's head is sent as given and creates are not deduplicated
given: a forge accepting a pull request and refusing a second for the same head and base
tests.when: a pull request is opened with a plain branch head, with an owner:branch head, and then created again for the same head and base
then: each head reaches the forge exactly as given
the duplicate is refused by the forge and answered 422 forge_rejected
the hub keeps no idempotency key, so a retried create that already succeeded creates a second
tests.pseudocode: in the forge writes integration test file: post(pulls, head='owner:b'); assert forge.lastBody.head == 'owner:b'

tests.title: Body-like fields are measured and nothing else is
given: a GitHub workspace and a GitLab workspace, and a recording forge
tests.when: each of the four body-like fields is sent at the limit and one code point over, with multi-byte characters, and an over-long title, head, base, label name and assignee are sent
then: each field at the limit is sent and each one over answers 413 body_too_large naming the length and the limit
the limits are 65536 on GitHub and 1000000 on GitLab
a multi-byte character counts as one code point
the over-long title, head, base, label name and assignee are sent to the forge
no request reaches the forge for a refused body and no event is recorded
tests.pseudocode: in the forge writes test file, table over (field, forgeKind, length, expected)

tests.title: Every forge failure maps to its documented answer
given: forges answering 404, 401, a non-rate-limit 403, another 4xx, a 5xx, an unreadable body, and a forge that cannot be connected to
tests.when: a read and a write are called against each
then: the statuses and error types are 404 forge_not_found, 502 forge_unauthenticated, 502 forge_forbidden, 422 forge_rejected, 502 forge_error, 502 forge_error and 502 forge_unreachable respectively
a read and a write map identically
tests.pseudocode: in the forge failures integration test file, table over (forgeBehaviour, expectedStatus, expectedErrorType)

tests.title: The forge's message is scrubbed, truncated and given its hint
given: a forge answering with a message containing the token and a URL with userinfo, and one answering a 2000-character message
a workspace with a username and password, and one with no credential
tests.when: a write is attempted against each
then: the message reads as the forge answering with its status
the token is replaced and the userinfo removed
the message is cut to 1024 bytes
the 401 for a basic credential adds the hint to store a token
the workspace with no credential answers 502 forge_error with nothing sent and no event recorded
tests.pseudocode: in the forge failures integration test file: r = post(write); assert TOKEN not in r.text and len(r.json.error.message) <= 1024

tests.title: A rate limit is waited out once, or refused with Retry-After
given: a forge rate-limiting with a 5-second wait then succeeding, one with a 200-second wait, one with a 29-second wait, and one giving no wait
tests.when: a read is called against each
then: the 5-second wait is taken and the retry's result is answered
the 200-second wait answers 429 forge_rate_limited with Retry-After in whole seconds rounded up
the 29-second wait is cut short by the deadline and answers 504 forge_timeout
the unknown wait answers 429 without a Retry-After
tests.pseudocode: in the forge failures integration test file, table over the four behaviours asserting the status, the error type and the Retry-After header

tests.title: No response or event carries a credential or userinfo
given: a workspace whose credential and whose remote URL userinfo are distinctive
every failure mode of every forge route
tests.when: each failure is produced and its response and recorded event are inspected
then: no response body contains the credential or the userinfo
no recorded event's metadata contains either
tests.pseudocode: in the forge failures test file, over every route and failure: assert CRED not in body and USERINFO not in body and CRED not in event.metadata

tests.title: A read route checks in the documented order
given: combinations where two checks would both fail: a PAT without the scope for a slug naming nothing, a bad target with a bad path number, and a bad path number on a workspace whose forge cannot be identified
tests.when: each combination is requested
then: the PAT without the scope answers 403 naming forge:read even for a slug that names nothing
the bad target is answered before the bad path number
the bad path number is answered before the unidentifiable forge
tests.pseudocode: in the forge order test file, table over (conditions, expectedAnswer)

tests.title: A write route checks in the documented order
given: a PAT holding only forge:read, a member, an archived workspace, a body that breaks a rule, a workspace whose forge cannot be identified, and an oversized body
tests.when: combinations are requested where two checks would both fail
then: the forge:read PAT answers 403 naming forge:write before the workspace is looked up
a member answers 403 forbidden
an archived workspace answers 400 before the body is validated
an oversized body on a workspace whose forge cannot be identified answers 422 forge_unknown rather than 413
tests.pseudocode: in the forge order test file, table over (conditions, expectedStatus, expectedErrorType)

tests.title: A refused forge request sends nothing and records nothing
given: a recording forge and a recording event store
tests.when: every refusal of every read and write route is produced
then: the forge received no request for any of them
no hub event was recorded for any of them
tests.pseudocode: in the forge order test file, over every refusal: assert forge.requests == 0 and events.recorded == 0

tests.title: An agent triages an issue against a running deployment
given: a running deployment, a workspace whose repository is on a real or stubbed forge with a stored credential
tests.when: afc issue list with a label filter, afc issue get and afc issue label are run in turn
then: the list returns the matching issues
the get returns the issue with its comments
the label write succeeds and the label is on the issue afterwards
one forge write event is recorded for the label write and none for the reads
tests.pseudocode: in the forge smoke test file: run('afc issue list --label af:triage'); run('afc issue get'); run('afc issue label'); assert events_for(workspace) has one forge write

tests.title: An agent opens a pull request upstream against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and a carry_patch workspace with an upstream repository, an upstream credential and a branch already pushed to it
tests.when: afc pr create --target upstream is run and then afc pr state --target upstream
then: the create answers 201 with the pull request
the upstream credential and the upstream API URL were used, not the origin's
the state read reports it open
tests.pseudocode: in the forge smoke test file: r = run('afc pr create --target upstream ...'); assert r.exit == 0 and json(run('afc pr state --target upstream').stdout).state == 'open'

tests.title: A rejected credential is reported without disclosing it
given: a running deployment and a workspace whose stored forge credential the forge rejects
tests.when: afc issue create is run
then: the command exits 1 and the envelope carries error_type forge_unauthenticated
the message carries the forge's scrubbed answer and the hint to store a token
no output contains the credential
one forge write event is recorded carrying that error type
tests.pseudocode: in the forge smoke test file: r = run('afc issue create ...'); assert r.exit == 1 and json(r.stdout).error.error_type == 'forge_unauthenticated' and CRED not in r.stdout
